title: Chapter XXVI
summary: At the altar, solicitor Briggs declares that Rochester already has a living wife. Richard Mason proves that Rochester married his sister Bertha in Jamaica fifteen years earlier. Rochester admits he intended bigamy and takes the party to Thornfield's third storey, where Bertha is confined under Grace Poole's care and violently attacks him. The apparent Grace Poole mystery, the fire, Mason's wounds, and the torn veil are finally unified. John Eyre, having learned of the marriage through Mason, supplied the intervention that saves Jane from an invalid union.
events: Briggs interrupts the ceremony by alleging an insuperable legal impediment.
Mason's statement and testimony establish that Bertha Antoinetta Mason Rochester is alive.
Rochester admits his plan and reveals Bertha confined in the hidden room at Thornfield.
Briggs explains that Jane's uncle learned the truth from Mason and arranged to stop the wedding.

characters.name: Jane Eyre
characters.development: Learns that her consent was obtained through material deception and stands outwardly composed as her expected identity collapses.

characters.name: Edward Rochester
characters.development: His attempt to override law and concealment fails; he admits bigamous intent while demanding judgment in light of his suffering.

characters.name: Bertha Mason Rochester
characters.development: Revealed as Rochester's living wife and the person behind Thornfield's fires, attacks, laughter, and torn veil.

characters.name: Richard Mason
characters.development: Acts with Briggs and John Eyre to make his sister's existence legally undeniable.

threads.text: Thornfield's mystery is identified as Bertha Mason Rochester, guarded by Grace Poole.
Mason's danger to Rochester is his ability to prove the existing marriage.
John Eyre acts as Jane's unknown protector but is gravely ill in Madeira.
Jane and Rochester's planned marriage is legally and morally stopped.
